pr_title: cryptsetup: fall back to traditional unlocking if any TPM2 operation fails
pr_body:
If any TPM2 operation fails, the boot process should continue and
prompt for a text password (if configured to do so).

Fixes #22870
pr_comments: So, for your specific DA lockout error I'd really prefer if we'd log a proper error though. i.e. in the tpm code propagate DA lockout as some recognizable error we so far don#t use. (EUCLEAN?) and then catch it here, and log explicitly that the TPM2 chip is dictionary attack lockout mode, and even better say something actionable, i.e. what to do to recover.

> So, for your specific DA lockout error I'd really prefer if we'd log a proper error though. i.e. in the tpm code propagate DA lockout as some recognizable error we so far don#t use. (EUCLEAN?) and then catch it here, and log explicitly that the TPM2 chip is dictionary attack lockout mode, and even better say something actionable, i.e. what to do to recover.

Ok, I'll create a separate commit with that.

I see the DA lockout error is already handled:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/81669507632e530e4c60b745f209a73fda2ddc21/src/shared/tpm2-util.c#L1115-L1137

But the error code I receive here is `0x1df`. I've been digging into the tpm2-tss library and couldn't find any define that expands to this value (neither in tss2_tpm2_types.h, nor in tss2_common.h)... I tried with every possible return value defined in Esys_Load.c, but no luck. Searching I only found references to this hex code directly (https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-tools/issues/2024#issuecomment-628711664)...

So I'm kind of stuck with what I could do here.

hmm, maybe the error code returned by your hw changed?

There's this `tpm2_rc_decode` tool in the tpm2_tools package, and it will decode 0x1df as:

```
$ tpm2_rc_decode 0x1df
tpm:parameter(1):integrity check failed
```

Maybe the rc code returnes by your tpm has changed since you first tested this? does the error dump still look the same as it did then? i.e. in your original log from #22870 we see this:

```
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: WARNING:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:324:Esys_Load_Finish() Received TPM Error
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: ERROR:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:112:Esys_Load() Esys Finish ErrorCode (0x00000921)
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: Failed to load HMAC key in TPM: tpm:warn(2.0): authorizations for objects subject to DA protection are not allowed at this time because the TPM is in DA lockout mode
```

Which suggests the error code you saw then is actually 0x921...  but now you say 0x1df? so did the code change in the meantime? Or did the tpm2 stack somehow mangle the error code from the lower layers to be something different now?

Yes, the log looks different. Every time I follow the steps described in the issue (rebooting after just calling `tpm2_clear`) I always get `0x1df`. I don't have an answer why now I always get this, but when I opened the issue I was running more tpm2 commands to test what was going on. I've just created a new vm and I keep getting the same error code.

```
localhost:/home/dev # systemctl status "systemd-cryptsetup@cr\x2dauto\x2d1.service"
● systemd-cryptsetup@cr\x2dauto\x2d1.service - Cryptography Setup for cr-auto-1
     Loaded: loaded (/etc/crypttab; generated)
     Active: active (exited) since Wed 2022-03-30 12:30:34 CEST; 1min 6s ago
       Docs: man:crypttab(5)
             man:systemd-cryptsetup-generator(8)
             man:systemd-cryptsetup@.service(8)
   Main PID: 495 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)
        CPU: 3.580s

Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd[1]: Starting Cryptography Setup for cr-auto-1...
Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: WARNING:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:324:Esys_Load_Finish() Received TPM Error
Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: ERROR:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:112:Esys_Load() Esys Finish ErrorCode (0x000001df)
Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: gotcha 0x1DF
Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: Set cipher aes, mode xts-plain64, key size 512 bits for device /dev/disk/by-uuid/274d583a->
Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: WARNING:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:324:Esys_Load_Finish() Received TPM Error
Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: ERROR:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:112:Esys_Load() Esys Finish ErrorCode (0x000001df)
Mar 30 12:30:27 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: gotcha 0x1DF
Mar 30 12:30:32 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[495]: Set cipher aes, mode xts-plain64, key size 512 bits for device /dev/disk/by-uuid/274d583a->
Mar 30 12:30:34 localhost systemd[1]: Finished Cryptography Setup for cr-auto-1.
```

That the TPM2_RC_LOCKOUT code was not handled in the issue report was my fault, the commit that added it was merged 15 days ago, so sorry for that.

DA lockout happens if you try to unlock via TPM too frequently. means "dictionary attack lockout". Thus, my guess is that the actual error you saw was that integrity failure thing, but then you tried this a couple of times, at which time you tried it too frequently and got the DA lockout error instead, until some time passed when you soo the original integrity failure thing.

so this all looks as something one can expect.

So the patch looks good too, just some nitpicking about log level, see above.

issue_context.title: systemd-cryptsetup does not ask for password if any TPM2 operation fails with ENOTRECOVERABLE
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > v250

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released *major* systemd versions upstream! -->
<!--           If there have been multiple stable releases for that major version, please consider updating to a recent one before reporting an issue. -->
<!--           When using a distro package, please make sure that the version reported is meaningful for upstream. -->
<!-- See https://github.com/systemd/systemd-stable/tags for the list of most recent releases. -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://systemd.io/CONTRIBUTING#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > openSUSE Tumbleweed

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > `Linux localhost.localdomain 5.16.15-1-default #1 SMP PREEMPT Wed Mar 16 23:33:05 UTC 2022 (d8f0e40) x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x86_64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Be able to boot the system by entering a text password if the TPM is cleared.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > Unable to boot.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 > 1. Example FS Layout (`cryptsetup luksFormat -y -v --type luks2 /dev/vda3`). 
```
dev@localhost:~> lsblk
NAME          MAJ:MIN RM   SIZE RO TYPE  MOUNTPOINTS
sr0            11:0    1 912.9M  0 rom   
vda           253:0    0    20G  0 disk  
├─vda1        253:1    0   512M  0 part  /boot/efi
├─vda2        253:2    0     2G  0 part  /boot
└─vda3        253:3    0  17.5G  0 part  
  └─cr-auto-1 254:0    0  17.5G  0 crypt /var
                                         /srv
                                         /root
                                         /home
                                         /opt
                                         /usr/local
                                         /
```
 > 2. `systemd-cryptenroll --tpm2-device=auto /dev/vda3`
 > 3. Add `tpm2-device=auto` to cr-auto-1 in /etc/crypttab
 > 4. Clear TPM SRK (run `tpm2_clear`)
 > 5. Reboot.

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**

<!-- Please paste relevant program terminal or journal output here, ideally
     when generated in debug mode (try setting the SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
     environment variable). For very long copy/pasted data consider using a
     service like https://gist.github.com/. Where copy/paste is not possible
     (for example early boot or late shutdown), a photo of the screen might do
     too, but text is always much preferred. -->
```text
sh-4.4# systemctl status "systemd-cryptsetup@cr\x2dauto\x2d1.service"
× systemd-cryptsetup@cr\x2dauto\x2d1.service - Cryptography Setup for cr-auto-1
     Loaded: loaded (/etc/crypttab; generated)
     Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since Thu 2022-03-24 08:01:35 UTC; 46min ago
       Docs: man:crypttab(5)
             man:systemd-cryptsetup-generator(8)
             man:systemd-cryptsetup@.service(8)
    Process: 404 ExecStart=/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-cryptsetup attach cr-auto-1 /dev/disk/by-uuid/7bb5cda8-0a95-42ef-b763-7386c5c72e49 none x-initrd.attach,tpm2-device=auto (code=exited, status=1/FAILURE)
   Main PID: 404 (code=exited, status=1/FAILURE)

Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd[1]: Starting Cryptography Setup for cr-auto-1...
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: Set cipher aes, mode xts-plain64, key size 512 bits for device /dev/disk/by-uuid/7bb5cda8-0a95-42ef-b763-7386c5c72e49.
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: Automatically discovered security TPM2 token unlocks volume.
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: WARNING:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:324:Esys_Load_Finish() Received TPM Error
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: ERROR:esys:src/tss2-esys/api/Esys_Load.c:112:Esys_Load() Esys Finish ErrorCode (0x00000921)
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd-cryptsetup[404]: Failed to load HMAC key in TPM: tpm:warn(2.0): authorizations for objects subject to DA protection are not allowed at this time because the TPM is in DA lockout mode
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd[1]: systemd-cryptsetup@cr\x2dauto\x2d1.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd[1]: systemd-cryptsetup@cr\x2dauto\x2d1.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Mar 24 08:01:35 localhost systemd[1]: Failed to start Cryptography Setup for cr-auto-1.
```

This happens in the `tpm2_unseal` method:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/e5531be27b034a7f4c517a0f76cbcbabe63c960e/src/shared/tpm2-util.c#L1132-L1135

Which is called from:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/e5531be27b034a7f4c517a0f76cbcbabe63c960e/src/cryptsetup/cryptsetup.c#L1328-L1338

Then ends here:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/e5531be27b034a7f4c517a0f76cbcbabe63c960e/src/cryptsetup/cryptsetup.c#L1906-L1909

Is the expected behavior not to continue with the boot process (and not prompt for password) if any of the TPM2 operations return ENOTRECOVERABLE?
comments: We should probably provide a proper log message about DA lockout mode. And yes, we should not fail completely, but try with a pw

review_comments: no braces around single-line if statements
